blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: `src/main.rs` accepts `--quiet` before the file and passes it to
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The progress reporter takes a `quiet` switch
findings.recommendation: State in the spec what `ledger import data.csv --quiet` (flag after the file) does, and add a scenario for it: either it is accepted like `--quiet data.csv`, or it is a usage error with exit code 2. Today `src/main.rs` matches the arguments positionally (`[command, path] if command == "import"`), so a nightly script that writes the flag after the file would get the usage line and exit 2 instead of a quiet import; the spec's only scenarios put the flag before the file.
findings.title: The flag's position on the command line is left unspecified

findings.evidence: - [ ] 1.1 `--quiet` read by `src/main.rs`, added to `FLAGS` in `src/cli/import.rs` and passed to `Progress::new(quiet)`, verified by tests `a_quiet_import_prints_nothing` ("A quiet import") and `a_quiet_import_still_prints_errors` ("A quiet import that fails")
findings.recommendation: Move the `FLAGS` entry into task 1.2 with the documentation, or have task 1.1's verification include `cargo test docs_mention_every_flag`. As ordered, once 1.1 is done `tests/docs.rs` iterates over `FLAGS`, finds `--quiet` absent from `docs/cli.md` and fails, so 1.1 cannot be checked as done with a green test suite.
findings.title: Task 1.1 adds the flag to `FLAGS` before its documentation exists, leaving the docs test red

findings.recommendation: Add to task 1.1 updating the usage line to `usage: ledger import [--quiet] <file>`, so that a user who gets the usage error (for instance by writing the flag in an unaccepted position, see R-skeptic-1) learns the flag exists; the plan updates `docs/cli.md` but not the only help the binary itself prints.
findings.title: The usage line printed by `src/main.rs` is not updated to mention `--quiet`
